name: mentions extra unrelated exceptions vs sticks to primary exception only
side_a: Credit answers limit their diagnosis to the exception directly caused by the cast (ClassCastException) and do not list other possible exceptions.
side_b: Deduct answers add speculation about additional exceptions that are not directly caused by the line, e.g., NullPointerException or SecurityException.

name: suggests generic try‑catch wrapping vs purely diagnostic description
side_a: Credit answers describe the exception risk without recommending additional try‑catch blocks.
side_b: Deduct answers explicitly recommend wrapping the code in try‑catch for robustness.

name: only‑ClassCastException mentioned vs mentions other exception types
side_a: Credit the answer when it mentions only ClassCastException as the possible failure (no other exception types are listed).
side_b: Deduct when the answer lists additional exception types (e.g., NullPointerException, SecurityException) or suggests generic try‑catch handling.

name: calls target an interface vs calls target a type
side_a: Credit the answer when it refers to OnKeyListenerForFragments as a *type* (e.g., “cast … to OnKeyListenerForFragments type”) without labeling it an interface.
side_b: Deduct when the answer explicitly calls OnKeyListenerForFragments an *interface* (e.g., “implement … interface”, “doesn’t implement the OnKeyListenerForFragments interface”).

name: explicitly‑states‑null‑cast‑safe vs no/incorrect mention of null‑cast safety
side_a: Credit the answer when it explicitly says that casting a null fragment is allowed and will not throw a ClassCastException (e.g., “the cast is still valid (as casting null is allowed)”).
side_b: Deduct when the answer either omits any comment on casting null or suggests that null could cause a ClassCastException or does not clarify that casting null is safe.

name: mentions null‑cast‑allowed vs does not mention it
side_a: Credit the answer when it never says that casting a null fragment is allowed or safe. No deduction.
side_b: Deduct when the answer explicitly states that casting a null result from findFragmentById is allowed (e.g., “casting null is allowed”).

name: mentions null‑check mitigation vs no null‑check mention
side_a: Credit the answer when it does not claim any mitigation for a missing fragment (no null‑check discussion).
side_b: Deduct when the answer points out that a subsequent null‑check prevents a NullPointerException after a missing fragment.

name: explicit cast location vs vague/no location
side_a: Credit when the answer explicitly identifies the cast of the fragment returned by `findFragmentById(R.id.main_view)` (e.g., “when casting the fragment to OnKeyListenerForFragments”) as the spot where an exception may be thrown.
side_b: Deduct when the answer does not mention the cast operation or the specific line, speaking only in generic terms about an exception.

name: named ClassCastException vs unnamed/other exception
side_a: Credit when the answer explicitly names `ClassCastException` as the likely exception caused by the cast.
side_b: Deduct when the answer either only says “exception” without naming it, or names a different exception (e.g., NullPointerException) as the primary risk.
